tested:
No entries existed for "vqfxre"/"vqfxpfe" (Juniper vQFX virtual switch: Routing
Engine + Packet Forwarding Engine, split the same way vMX splits into VCP/VFP) -
both fell through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (512MB RAM, disk_bus="virtio"). Same two-
tables-drifted class as barracuda/sonicwall/csp-vpn-gate/vmx above: image_profiles.py
already has "vqfxre": ("ide", ...) and "vqfxpfe": ("ide", ...). Found 2026-07-23 with
DIRECT live evidence, not just the vendor minimum: a real vqfxre node hit 1970MB of
actual usage against the old 512MB cap (385% - host-guard's hypervisor RAM cap kept
it alive but starved). Juniper's own published vQFX minimum is 1024MB per component;
default_ram_mb set to 2048 for both - comfortably above both the published minimum
and the observed 1970MB real usage.
boot_timeout_sec raised 360 -> 1500 (Wave 21 U6, 2026-09-07): a live isolated repro
of vqfxre-10K-F-20.3R1.8 (needed 2 attempts to get a trustworthy read - see the
tracker's Wave 21 U6 vqfxre subsection for the two contaminated/false-positive
attempts first) showed a genuine console `login:` prompt at t=937.5s, syslog noise
settling by t=946.7s, then a fully idle console (only telnet keepalive NOPs) out to
t=1775s with zero further boot text - i.e. the real boot-to-login time is ~950-960s,
nearly 3x the old 360s cap. 1500s gives ~550s of margin above the observed time,
consistent with this file's margin convention for other slow-booting devices.

reasons.day0_channel:
NPX-1213 ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-09-16): the earlier attempt tagged this
profile with "juniper-config-drive" (JuniperConfigDriveChannel) and hit a
real, reproducible 25+ minute hang with zero console output. That channel
was simply the WRONG one for this device - its own sibling class,
JuniperCdromMountChannel, documents in its own docstring (day0_channels.py)
that "vmx/vqfxre use /dev/vtbd0", i.e. this exact image belongs to the
typed-mount family (5-command mount+cli+configure+load-set+commit sequence,
disk attached as bus="virtio"/device="disk"), NOT the auto-read family
(JuniperConfigDriveChannel, disk attached as bus="sata"/device="cdrom" -
confirmed the likely real cause of the hang: this profile's machine type is
"pc" (i440fx) with a primary disk already on disk_bus="ide", and a SECOND,
sata-bus cdrom forces libvirt to add an AHCI controller SeaBIOS then hangs
probing). "juniper-cdrom-mount-vtbd0" is the correct, already-existing
registry entry: since this profile's own disk_bus is "ide" (not "virtio"),
the day0 channel's virtio-bus disk is the FIRST virtio block device the
guest sees, i.e. /dev/vtbd0 - matching the exact device the channel's own
docstring names for this family (same reasoning that makes vsrx, whose
primary disk_bus IS "virtio", correctly use vtbd1 instead - its day0 disk is
the SECOND virtio device once the primary one is already vtbd0).
